CAPACITY MATH (at the measured 3.04 s/page)
THROUGHPUT floor one slot = 3600 / 3.04 = 1,184 pages/hour 72,000 / 1,184 = 61 slots
LATENCY requirement case wall clock ~25s, arrivals every 30s => ~10 cases in flight x 10 docs each = 100 doc-slots
SIZE FOR LATENCY — it dominates. Throughput is then free (100 slots = 20k docs/h vs 12k needed).

DERIVED FLEET @ 3.04 s/page
IDP 100 doc-slots -> 25-50 pods (c=2-4 per GPU) -> 25-50 GPU nodes Reasoning 13 concurrent -> 2-4 pods (c=100) Assembly ~1 concurrent -> 2 pods (HA only) API 3 pods Ingestion 1 active (Lease) + 1 standby
Slots-per-GPU is the open variable: models are ~400 MB so VRAM is not the limit, COMPUTE is.

SAME FLEET @ 1.5 s/page (CUDA — ESTIMATED)
a 6-page doc drops 18.2s -> ~9s, so a slot turns over twice as fast
IDP -> ~50 doc-slots -> 13-25 GPU nodes every other tier unchanged (none are the bottleneck)
HALVES THE GPU BILL — the single biggest cost lever. Verify before budgeting (§9.6, §9.7).

KEDA ScaledObject dgcl-idp trigger: redis listName=q.idp listLength=5 min 2 · max 50 · cooldown 300s min is NEVER 0: 4s model load + ~4 GB image pull
KEDA ScaledObject dgcl-reasoning trigger: redis listName=q.reason listLength=20 min 2 · max 40 · cooldown 120s can scale fast and wide: 50 MB, pure HTTP wait
Cluster Autoscaler / Karpenter GPU group scales AFTER KEDA marks pods Pending node provision ~2-4 min + ~2 min image pull => keep warm headroom; do not scale to the floor
SCALE-UP LAG IS THE REAL RISK A 10x burst needs new GPU nodes: ~5 min before the first pod is Ready. Queue absorbs it only if the SLA tolerates ~5 min of backlog. Otherwise: over-provision the floor.
ElastiCache Redis (cache.m6g.large, multi-AZ) steady state depth ~0 — a rising depth IS the alert burst: 100 messages per poll (10 cases x 10 docs) alert on q.idp OLDEST AGE, not depth
RDS PostgreSQL (db.t4g.medium, multi-AZ) 1,200 rows/hour = ~29k/day = ~10M/year trivial load — this tier will never be the limit sized for HA and audit retention, not throughput

S3 ~12 MB per case (raw + extracted + structured + result) = ~14 GB/hour · ~345 GB/day · ~126 TB/year LIFECYCLE POLICY IS MANDATORY: raw -> IA at 30d, Glacier at 90d. Results stay hot for the review UI.

The only tier that grows without bound is S3. Everything else is steady-state.
Budget the object count too, not just bytes: ~50 objects/case = 60k/hour = 500M/year.
1 · GPU node count The binding constraint and ~all of the cost. 74% of per-page time is OCR (§1.5) and it is the only stage still on CPU. Fix that first and this ladder shifts by one rung.
2 · LLM provider rate limit 12,000 documents/hour of extraction calls. At 1 call/doc that is 3.3 req/s sustained — check the tier limit. Batching 5-10 docs per call drops it to ~0.5 req/s.
3 · Scale-up lag, not capacity ~5 min from burst to first Ready GPU pod. A spiky arrival pattern hits this long before it hits steady-state capacity.
4 · S3 object count / lifecycle ~500M objects/year. Not a throughput limit, but a cost and listing-performance problem if no lifecycle policy exists.
NOT bottlenecks Postgres — trivial load Redis — steady depth ~0 API / assembly tiers — milliseconds Ingestion — 2 API calls per 30s
